findings.title: Duplicate method definition of self.downsize silently overrides the first
findings.body: Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined with different signatures (one taking max_width/max_height, one taking dimensions string). Ruby allows this but the second definition completely overrides the first, meaning the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` signature is dead code and any caller using that 4-arg form will get a wrong number of arguments error or silently broken behavior. This is likely unintentional leftover code that should be removed.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit ignores SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb
findings.body: The download size limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Since the PR introduces automatic downsizing specifically to allow larger uploads beyond max_image_size_kb, this works for the resize feature, but it silently changes behavior for admins who configured a smaller or larger value for max_image_size_kb-based downloads unrelated to the resize retry loop, and removes configurability. If this is intentional it should be documented, but currently it's an undocumented behavior change with no corresponding site setting.

findings.title: Downsize loop can silently fail or infinite small-step reduce without catching errors
findings.body: The resize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times reducing to 80% each time, but if `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (returns false, e.g. ImageMagick error) the loop doesn't check the return value, it just decrements attempt and tries again overwriting the same file. If the tool fails on the first iteration, the tempfile could become corrupted or zero-byte, and the code would still proceed to use it in `Upload.create_for`, with `content_type` possibly stale/mismatched to the now-corrupted file, producing invalid or broken uploads without any error being surfaced to the user.

findings.title: Hardcoded max upload size removes site-setting-driven configurability
findings.body: Both `validateUploadedFile` and `displayErrorForUpload` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to determine file size limits, but now hardcode 10MB. This breaks the API/contract for admins who have configured different max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb values — client-side validation will now be inconsistent with server-side settings, giving users misleading error messages (e.g., showing 10MB limit when server actually allows uploads up to a different size via the new downsizing feature, or rejects differently).
